_doc: Store ▸ Cloud: the buttons a fleet row's detail offers, IN ORDER, on TWO lines, with their captions and colours. The Kotlin only maps an id to what it does (StoreCloudFragment.rowAction / ApkDetailSheet.detailAction); order, wording and grouping are this file. #redesign split the single button strip into two grouped lines: `rows[0]` is the install/lifecycle line (Download · Install⇄Uninstall · Direct Install · Clear), `rows[1]` the open/inspect line (Open · Stop │ Perms · Routes · Libs · About · Access). `install_toggle` is ONE button that shows `label` when the package is absent and `label_installed` when it is present, and runs the matching action (prompted system-sheet install, via BootstrapInstall, when absent; Uninstall when present). `direct_install` is the SILENT path (StoreStages' cached install, downgrade-gated — the store's own installer, no system sheet). `divider_before` draws the owner's `│` rule before a button, grouping Open/Stop apart from the Perms/Routes/Libs/About/Access inspect set. The five inspect ids open sub-sheets over the page (nav bar and back stay — they never replace the bottom nav): Perms (Manifest / Auto grants / Runtime tables), Routes (MCP · IPC · API tabs), Libs (compiled-in + bound engines), About (the full detail sheet, ApkDetailSheet, which supersedes the old `details` button), Access (the per-app access surface — MCP · API · IPC · ID · Perms tabs, StoreInspect.Access over StoreAccess, reading the same registry projections Routes does). Stop goes through the fleet's EXISTING privileged door — ShellChannels — and says so with no channel armed. test-store-fleet-actions.sh holds the two-line shape, the toggle, the divider, and that every id has a handler; test-store-inspect.sh holds the four inspect sheets and their data sources.
_doc_fields: id = the verb the code dispatches on; label = the caption drawn; color = the button fill (ARGB hex). `label_installed`/`color_installed` = the toggle's caption/fill while the package is installed. `divider_before` = draw a `│` rule before this button. The `details` entries feed the About sheet's Actions card (ApkDetailSheet.detailAction); each carries `detail`, the right-hand hint on the sheet's action line.
